To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the 12Gleu9 polymorphism of the gene encoding the alpha 2B adrenergic receptor was associated with impaired first phase insulin secretion and with increased risk of developing type 2 diabetes in patients with impaired glucose tolerance not subjected to lifestyle intervention, whereas this polymorphism was not associated with these outcomes in patients with impaired tolerance subjected to lifestyle intervention.

The 12Glu/9 polymorphism in ADRA2B was associated with impaired first phase insulin secretion and predicted the development of Type-2 diabetes in subjects who were not subjected to lifestyle intervention.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the role of the α2B adrenergic receptor in the regulation of insulin secretion and its role as a risk factor for the development of type 2 diabetes.
the role of the adrenergic system in the pathogenesis of Type 2 Diabetes.
the study of the molecular mechanisms underlying the pathogenesis of diabetes mellitus.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this study suggests that the 12Gle9 polymorphism of the α2B adrenergic receptor is a risk factor for Type 2 diabetes mellitus.
the ADRA2B 12Glu/9 polymorphism may predict the development and/or the progression of Type 2 DM, and this may be mediated via its effects on the first phase insulin secretion.
this polymorphism may have a role in the development of Type-2 diabetes mellitus.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
this polymorphism is associated with impaired insulin secretion and may be a risk factor for Type 2 diabetes, especially in subjects with impaired insulin secretion.
the Glu9 variant of ADRA2β may be associated with a lower acute insulin response and may predict the risk of diabetes in subjects with IGT who are not subjected a lifestyle intervention.
the ADRA2B 12Glu/9 polymorphism is associated with impaired insulin secretion, but only in the absence of weight loss.
The main takeaway from our work is that
this polymorphism is a marker for the development of diabetes in people with IGT, but not in people with diabetes.
the 12Gleu9 polymorphism in ADRA2B may be a useful genetic marker to identify individuals with impaired first-phase secretion who are at risk of developing Type-2 diabetes.
the 12Gly9 polymorphism of α2B-adrenoceptor is associated with insulin secretory capacity in individuals with IGT.
